THE NON-CONSTRUCTED "I": THE ARGUMENT AGAINST THE SELF-MODEL

How the IPVV proves the self-grasp is intrinsic — the three-kinds-of-construction argument and its defeat of the higher-order theory

  • 026-08-11. The contemporary philosophy of mind offers a powerful account of the self: the "I" is a
  • lf-model — a higher-order representation the system constructs of itself. The IPVV contains a direct
  • gument against this. It shows that the "I"-grasp (ahaṃ-pratyavamarśa) is not a construction at all:
  • nstruction is the joining of distinct things, the multiplication of a one, or the splitting off of a
  • ubted other — and the "I"-grasp is none of these. It is the self-presence that every construction
  • esupposes. This essay reconstructs the argument in full, applies it to the self-model theory and to
  • ṇavīra's structural reflexivity, and draws out its consequence: recognition is not the revision of a
  • del but the re-positioning of a self-grasp that was never constructed.*

1. The rival: the "I" as a construction

  • e strongest modern account of the self is the self-model: the "I" is a higher-order representation
  • e system constructs of itself — a model of the organism as a unified agent, built by the very
  • ocesses it represents. On this view, the "I" is a construction: an operation of joining, of
  • tributing, of representing one's own states. Reflexivity, on this view, is structural — experience
  • lds back and includes its own occurrence, and this folding is all the self there is.
  • ṇavīra, in the modern Pāli tradition, states this with great force, and adds a warning aimed
  • ecisely at the Pratyabhijñā: that Abhinavagupta "converted the reflexive self-identity of a
  • nditioned structure into an ultimately existing universal Self." The self is a conditioned structure
  • at folds back on itself; it is not an intrinsic, pre-existing substance.
  • e IPVV's argument (V2L) is a direct answer to this. It does not deny that the folding occurs; it
  • nies that the folding is the root.

2. The argument: the three kinds of construction

  • e IPVV defines construction with precision (V2L):
"The construction is of three kinds: it joins what is distinct (as one joins molasses, curd, and
pepper); it constructs the one in many ways; or it splits off a doubted, other form. All three are
operations of division and joining, of this-and-that."
  • at is, a construction (vikalpa) is:
  • Joining what is distinct (synthesizing a compound out of parts).
  • Multiplying the one into many (constructing one thing in many ways).
  • Splitting off a doubted other (dividing off a questionable form).
  • l three are operations on parts — operations of division and joining, of this-and-that.
  • w the "I"-grasp, the IPVV shows, is none of these:
"But the 'I'-recollection is none of these. It does not join a distinct 'this' to a distinct 'I'; it
is the single self-grasp, resting in itself. It is the pure self-awareness that underlies every
construction, the very thing that makes construction possible, without itself being one."
  • e three-fold proof:
  • Not joining. The "I"-grasp does not join a distinct "this" to a distinct "I" — it is not "this
  • built from a distinct "this" and "I." It is the single self-grasp.
  • Not multiplying. The "I"-grasp does not construct the one into many — it is the one.
  • Not splitting. The "I"-grasp does not split off a doubted other — it is the un-doubted
  • undation.
  • The conclusion.** The "I"-grasp is not a construction. And because every higher-order operation is a
  • ining or a splitting, the "I"-grasp cannot be a higher-order operation at all. It is the self-presence
  • at higher-order operations presuppose — the root that makes construction possible without itself being
  • e.

4. The application to Ñāṇavīra's structural reflexivity

  • ṇavīra's structural reflexivity — experience folding back and including itself — is, in the IPVV's
  • rms, a construction-capacity: it is the higher-order operation, the folding, the re-representation.
  • e IPVV does not deny this capacity exists. It denies that it is the root.
  • The reconciliation.** Structural reflexivity (the folding) is the construction-capacity; intrinsic
  • lf-manifestation (the "I"-grasp) is the self-grasp that the folding presupposes. They are not rivals;
  • ey are two levels. Ñāṇavīra describes the capacity (the folding); the IPVV points to what the folding

  • lf-presence that makes the folding possible, without itself being one.
  • The answer to the warning.** Ñāṇavīra's warning — that Abhinavagupta converts the reflexive identity

  • t (the "I"-grasp is not a construction), but it does not, from this alone, prove the numerical
  • entity of all "I"-grasps. The intrinsic-ness of each is established; the universality is a separate
  • gument.

  • 2C: the no-counter-correlate) and remains the commitment. Ñāṇavīra's warning is not fully closed by

5. Why this matters for recognition

  • e non-constructed "I" is the ground of the possibility of recognition. If the "I" were a
  • nstruction, recognition could only construct a new "I" — it could not re-cognize the one that is. The
  • VV's argument shows the "I" is not a construction, so recognition can re-position a self-grasp that
  • s never built.
  • d this is why recognition is not the revision of a self-model. The σ-flip (from the mechanism essay)
  • not a change in the model's self-attributions; it is a change in the self-positioning of the
  • lf-grasp that the model presupposes. Recognition removes the identification with the finite
  • lf-positioning — not by revising the model but by re-positioning the self-grasp that the model serves.
  • e self-model theory explains the content; the IPVV explains the self-grasp; recognition operates on
  • e self-grasp.

6. The precise statement of the argument

  • e IPVV's argument against the self-model, completely stated:
  • P1.** A construction is an operation of joining distinct things, multiplying a one into many, or
  • litting off a doubted other (V2L).
  • P2.** Every higher-order operation — every model, every self-attribution, every re-description — is a
  • ining or a splitting (i.e., a construction).
  • P3.** The "I"-grasp is none of these: it does not join (it is the single self-grasp), does not
  • ltiply (it is the one), does not split (it is the un-doubted foundation).
  • C1.** Therefore the "I"-grasp is not a construction (V2L).
  • C2.** Therefore the "I"-grasp is not a higher-order operation; it is the self-presence that
  • gher-order operations presuppose.
  • C3.** Therefore the self-model (a higher-order construction) cannot be the root of the "I"; it
  • plains the content, not the self-grasp.
  • C4.** (Honest remainder) This proves intrinsic reflexivity per act; it does not prove the numerical
  • entity of all "I"-grasps (the universalization is the separate commitment).

7. The boundary
